## Duty to restrict expert evidence

## 35.1

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.1] Expert evidence shall be restricted to that which is reasonably required to resolve the proceedings.

## Interpretation and definitions

## 35.2

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.2] (1) A reference to an ‘expert’ in this Part is a reference to a person who has been instructed to give or prepare expert evidence for the purpose of proceedings.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.2] (2) ‘Single joint expert’ means an expert instructed to prepare a report for the court on behalf of two or more of the parties (including the claimant) to the proceedings.

## Experts – overriding duty to the court

## 35.3

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.3] (1) It is the duty of experts to help the court on matters within their expertise.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.3] (2) This duty overrides any obligation to the person from whom experts have received instructions or by whom they are paid.

## Court’s power to restrict expert evidence

## 35.4

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (1) No party may call an expert or put in evidence an expert’s report without the court’s permission.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (2) When parties apply for permission they must provide an estimate of the costs of the proposed expert evidence and identify –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (a) the field in which expert evidence is required and the issues which the expert evidence will address; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (b) where practicable, the name of the proposed expert.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (3) If permission is granted it shall be in relation only to the expert named or the field identified under paragraph (2). The order granting permission may specify the issues which the expert evidence should address.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (3A) Where a claim has been allocated to the small claims track or the fast track, if permission is given for expert evidence, it will normally be given for evidence from only one expert on a particular issue.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (3B) In a soft tissue injury claim, permission—

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (a) may normally only be given for one expert medical report;

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (b) may not be given initially unless the medical report is a fixed cost medical report. Where the claimant seeks permission to obtain a further medical report, if the report is from a medical expert in any of the following disciplines—

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (i) Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon;

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (ii) Consultant in Accident and Emergency Medicine;

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (iii) General Practitioner registered with the General Medical Council; or

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (iv) Physiotherapist registered with the Health and Care Professions Council, the report must be a fixed cost medical report.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (3C) In a claim for a whiplash injury, whether or not it is part of a claim for other injuries—

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (a) permission—

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (i) may normally only be given for one expert medical report in respect of the claim for the whiplash injury; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (ii) may not be given initially unless the medical report is a fixed cost medical report; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (b) where the claimant seeks permission to obtain a further medical report in respect of the claim for the whiplash injury only, the report must be a fixed cost medical report if the report is from a medical expert in any of the following disciplines—

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (i) Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon;

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (ii) Consultant in Accident and Emergency Medicine;

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (iii) General Practitioner registered with the General Medical Council; or

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (iv) Physiotherapist registered with the Health and Care Professions Council.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (3D) Where, in respect of a claim for a whiplash injury, the claimant lives outside England and Wales, but chooses to be examined in England or Wales, paragraph (3C) applies.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (3E) Where the claimant obtains a medical report in respect of a more serious injury suffered on the same occasion as the whiplash injury, the claimant may be given permission to use that report instead of a fixed cost medical report under paragraph (3C) provided that—

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (a) the report is from a doctor who is listed on the General Medical Council’s Specialist Register; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (b) the report provides evidence of the whiplash injury.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (3F) Unless paragraph (3D) applies, where, in respect of a claim for a whiplash injury—

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (a) the claimant lives outside England and Wales;

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (b) permission is given for a medical report,

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] the medical report (or, if there is more than one report, the first report) must be obtained from a person who is recognised by the country in which they practise as—

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (i) being a medical expert; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (ii) having the required medical qualifications for the purposes of diagnosis and prognosis of a whiplash injury.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (3G) In this rule—

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (a) in respect of a soft tissue injury claim, ‘fixed cost medical report’ and ‘soft tissue injury claim’ have the meanings ascribed to them by paragraph 1.1(10A) and (16A), respectively, of the Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (b) in respect of a claim for a whiplash injury, ‘fixed cost medical report’ and ‘whiplash injury’ have the meanings ascribed to them by paragraph 1.2(17) and (38), respectively, of the Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims Below the Small Claims Limit in Road Traffic Accidents

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.4] (4) The court may limit the amount of a party’s expert’s fees and expenses that may be recovered from any other party.

## General requirement for expert evidence to be given in a written report

## 35.5

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.5] (1) Expert evidence is to be given in a written report unless the court directs otherwise.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.5] (2) If a claim is on the small claims track or the fast track, the court will not direct an expert to attend a hearing unless it is necessary to do so in the interests of justice.

## Written questions to experts

## 35.6

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (1) A party may put written questions about an expert’s report (which must be proportionate) to –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (a) an expert instructed by another party; or

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (b) a single joint expert appointed under rule 35.7.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (2) Written questions under paragraph (1) –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (a) may be put once only;

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (b) must be put within 28 days of service of the expert’s report; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (c) must be for the purpose only of clarification of the report,

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] unless in any case –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (i) the court gives permission; or

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (ii) the other party agrees.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (3) An expert’s answers to questions put in accordance with paragraph (1) shall be treated as part of the expert’s report.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (4) Where –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (a) a party has put a written question to an expert instructed by another party; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (b) the expert does not answer that question,

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] the court may make one or both of the following orders in relation to the party who instructed the expert –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (i) that the party may not rely on the evidence of that expert; or

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.6] (ii) that the party may not recover the fees and expenses of that expert from any other party.

## Court’s power to direct that evidence is to be given by a single joint expert

## 35.7

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.7] (1) Where two or more parties wish to submit expert evidence on a particular issue, the court may direct that the evidence on that issue is to be given by a single joint expert.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.7] (2) Where the parties who wish to submit the evidence (‘the relevant parties’) cannot agree who should be the single joint expert, the court may –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.7] (a) select the expert from a list prepared or identified by the relevant parties; or

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.7] (b) direct that the expert be selected in such other manner as the court may direct.

## Instructions to a single joint expert

## 35.8

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.8] (1) Where the court gives a direction under rule 35.7 for a single joint expert to be used, any relevant party may give instructions to the expert.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.8] (2) When a party gives instructions to the expert that party must, at the same time, send a copy to the other relevant parties.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.8] (3) The court may give directions about –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.8] (a) the payment of the expert’s fees and expenses; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.8] (b) any inspection, examination or experiments which the expert wishes to carry out.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.8] (4) The court may, before an expert is instructed –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.8] (a) limit the amount that can be paid by way of fees and expenses to the expert; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.8] (b) direct that some or all of the relevant parties pay that amount into court.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.8] (5) Unless the court otherwise directs, the relevant parties are jointly and severally liable (GL) for the payment of the expert’s fees and expenses.

## Power of court to direct a party to provide information

## 35.9

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.9] Where a party has access to information which is not reasonably available to another party, the court may direct the party who has access to the information to –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.9] (a) prepare and file a document recording the information; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.9] (b) serve a copy of that document on the other party.

## Contents of report

## 35.10

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.10] (1) An expert’s report must comply with the requirements set out in Practice Direction 35.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.10] (2) At the end of an expert’s report there must be a statement that the expert understands and has complied with their duty to the court.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.10] (3) The expert’s report must state the substance of all material instructions, whether written or oral, on the basis of which the report was written.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.10] (4) The instructions referred to in paragraph (3) shall not be privileged (GL) against disclosure but the court will not, in relation to those instructions –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.10] (a) order disclosure of any specific document; or

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.10] (b) permit any questioning in court, other than by the party who instructed the expert,

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.10] unless it is satisfied that there are reasonable grounds to consider the statement of instructions given under paragraph (3) to be inaccurate or incomplete.

## Use by one party of expert’s report disclosed by another

## 35.11

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.11] Where a party has disclosed an expert’s report, any party may use that expert’s report as evidence at the trial.

## Discussions between experts

## 35.12

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.12] (1) The court may, at any stage, direct a discussion between experts for the purpose of requiring the experts to –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.12] (a) identify and discuss the expert issues in the proceedings; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.12] (b) where possible, reach an agreed opinion on those issues.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.12] (2) The court may specify the issues which the experts must discuss.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.12] (3) The court may direct that following a discussion between the experts they must prepare a statement for the court setting out those issues on which –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.12] (a) they agree; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.12] (b) they disagree, with a summary of their reasons for disagreeing.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.12] (4) The content of the discussion between the experts shall not be referred to at the trial unless the parties agree.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.12] (5) Where experts reach agreement on an issue during their discussions, the agreement shall not bind the parties unless the parties expressly agree to be bound by the agreement.

## Consequence of failure to disclose expert’s report

## 35.13

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.13] A party who fails to disclose an expert’s report may not use the report at the trial or call the expert to give evidence orally unless the court gives permission.

## Expert’s right to ask court for directions

## 35.14

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.14] (1) Experts may file written requests for directions for the purpose of assisting them in carrying out their functions.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.14] (2) Experts must, unless the court orders otherwise, provide copies of the proposed requests for directions under paragraph (1) –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.14] (a) to the party instructing them, at least 7 days before they file the requests; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.14] (b) to all other parties, at least 4 days before they file them.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.14] (3) The court, when it gives directions, may also direct that a party be served with a copy of the directions.

## Assessors

## 35.15

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.15] (1) This rule applies where the court appoints one or more persons under section 70 of the Senior Courts Act 1981 1 or section 63 of the County Courts Act 1984 2 as an assessor.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.15] (2) An assessor will assist the court in dealing with a matter in which the assessor has skill and experience.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.15] (3) An assessor will take such part in the proceedings as the court may direct and in particular the court may direct an assessor to –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.15] (a) prepare a report for the court on any matter at issue in the proceedings; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.15] (b) attend the whole or any part of the trial to advise the court on any such matter.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.15] (4) If an assessor prepares a report for the court before the trial has begun –

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.15] (a) the court will send a copy to each of the parties; and

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.15] (b) the parties may use it at trial.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.15] (5) The remuneration to be paid to an assessor is to be determined by the court and will form part of the costs of the proceedings.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.15] (6) The court may order any party to deposit in the court office a specified sum in respect of an assessor’s fees and, where it does so, the assessor will not be asked to act until the sum has been deposited.

[PART 35 – EXPERTS AND ASSESSORS > 35.15] (7) Paragraphs (5) and (6) do not apply where the remuneration of the assessor is to be paid out of money provided by Parliament.
